st: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with water and add [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Cook for 10 minutes, then lay the chopped kale and onion on top of the potatoes.
Cover and cook for another 10 to 12 minutes until the potatoes are fork-tender and the kale is soft.
Meanwhile, simmer the sausage in a separate pot of hot water for 15 minutes until heated through (165°F/74°C).
Drain the potatoes and kale well, then return them to the pot.
Add the butter and mash roughly with a masher, leaving some texture.
Stir in the warm milk, nutmeg, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper until creamy.
Slice the sausage and serve it on top of the stamppot with a spoonful of mustard.
Put the peas, pork, water and bay leaf in a large heavy pot. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring now and then so the peas do not stick.
Add the onion, carrots, celery and potato and simmer for 30 minutes more.
Add the leeks and cook for 15 minutes until everything is soft.
Lift out the pork, cut away the meat and bones, and chop the meat. The pork should be well past 145°F (63°C) and tender.
Mash some of the soup with a spoon or briefly blend a small part to thicken it, then return the pork to the pot.
Slice the sausage, add it to the soup and simmer for 10 minutes until hot (165°F/74°C).
Season with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. The soup should be thick enough that a spoon almost stands up.
Serve hot with rye bread and bacon if you like.
Simmer the beef in the broth for about 1.5 hours until very tender. Lift out the beef, shred it very finely and keep [[2 cups]] of the broth.
Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] flour and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Slowly pour in the warm broth and milk, whisking, until you have a very thick smooth sauce.
Add the beef, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes. The mix should be stiff.
Spread the ragout in a dish, cover and chill for at least 3 hours until completely firm.
Scoop walnut-sized pieces and roll into balls with floured hands.
Roll each ball in the remaining flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. For a thicker crust, dip in egg and crumbs a second time.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry in small batches for 3 minutes until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mustard. The centers will be very hot.
Simmer the beef in the broth for about 1.5 hours until tender. Lift out the beef, shred it finely and keep [[2 cups]] of the broth.
Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the warm broth and milk slowly, whisking, until thick and smooth.
Mix in the beef, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until very thick.
Spread in a dish, cover and chill for at least 3 hours until firm.
Divide into 6 to 8 portions and shape each into a log about 4 inches long, using floured hands.
Roll each log in the remaining flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, and repeat the egg and crumbs for a thick crust.
Fry in oil heated to 350°F (175°C) for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mustard on bread or a plate.
Put the beef, broth, bay leaf and [[1 tsp]] salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour until the beef is very tender.
While the beef cooks, put the potatoes, carrots and onions in a separate large pot with water to cover and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Boil for 20 to 25 minutes until all vegetables are very soft.
Drain the vegetables, keeping a little cooking water.
Add the butter and mash to a chunky puree, adding a splash of cooking water if too dry.
Season with the remaining salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Serve the mash with the beef on top and spoon some of the beef broth over it as gravy.

ing: from a fishmonger, frozen first for at least 24 hours for safety
st: Buy herring that is sold as ready to eat, or use fillets that were frozen solid for at least 24 hours at 0°F (-18°C) or colder to kill parasites.
Thaw the fillets in the fridge, then pat dry with paper towels.
Finely chop the onion and rinse it under cold water for 20 seconds, then drain well.
Slice the pickles into thin rounds.
Arrange the fillets on a plate and scatter the onion over them.
Serve with the pickle slices and lemon wedges.
Eat by hand or tuck the herring into split rolls with onion and pickle.

ing: melted, plus more for the pan
st: Whisk the flours, yeast, sugar and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the lukewarm milk and egg and whisk into a smooth, thick batter.
Cover and let rest in a warm spot for 45 minutes until bubbly.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] melted butter.
Heat a poffertjes pan or a nonstick skillet with a few small dimples over medium heat and brush with butter.
Spoon or pipe small rounds of batter, about [[1 tbsp]] each, into the pan.
Cook for about 1 minute until bubbles form on top, then flip with a fork or skewer.
Cook the second side for 1 minute until puffed and golden.
Serve warm with a slab of butter and a thick dusting of powdered sugar.

ing: melted, plus more for the pan
st: Whisk the flour, sugar and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the middle.
Add the eggs and a splash of milk and whisk, slowly adding the rest of the milk until the batter is smooth.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] melted butter and let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
If using bacon, cook it in a large skillet until crisp, then keep the fat in the pan and set the bacon aside.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and brush with butter.
Pour in a ladle of batter and tilt the pan so it spreads thin and wide.
Add a few bacon pieces or cheese on top while the top is still wet, if using.
Cook for 2 minutes until the edges lift, then flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking pancakes on a warm plate. Serve with syrup.

ing: dark corn syrup or golden syrup
st: Mix the yeast with the warm milk and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Beat the softened butter with [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar until creamy, then add the egg.
Add the flour, cinnamon, salt and yeast mixture and knead into a smooth soft dough.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 balls, each about the size of a golf ball.
Heat a pizzelle iron or a waffle cone maker. Press one ball for 30 to 60 seconds until golden, then slice the hot waffle in half horizontally with a sharp knife right away.
Melt the syrup butter, [[1 cup]] brown sugar, syrup and cinnamon in a pan over medium heat. Simmer for 3 minutes, stirring, and cool for a few minutes.
Spread a spoonful of warm caramel on one waffle half and top with the other half. Press gently.
Let cool a few minutes so the filling sets. Repeat with the rest.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9 inch springform pan.
Mix the flour, [[0.75 cup]] sugar, baking powder and salt, then rub in the cold butter with your fingers until crumbly.
Add the egg and press the dough together. Chill for 30 minutes.
Toss the apples with [[0.33 cup]] sugar, raisins, cinnamon and lemon juice.
Press about two thirds of the dough into the pan to cover the bottom and 2 inches up the sides. Sprinkle the base with breadcrumbs.
Pile in the apple filling, pressing it down.
Roll out the rest of the dough and cut it into strips. Lay them in a lattice over the apples and press the edges to seal.
Brush the lattice with beaten egg yolk.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes until golden and the apples are tender.
Cool for at least 30 minutes before unmolding. Serve warm or cold with whipped cream.
Mix the mayonnaise, garlic, lemon juice and parsley in a small bowl for the garlic sauce. Chill until needed.
Pat the fish chunks very dry and season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, paprika and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Whisk in the egg and cold milk until you have a smooth batter that coats a spoon.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip fish pieces in the batter, let the extra drip off, then lower them into the oil a few at a time.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and the fish flakes easily (145°F/63°C inside).
Drain on paper towels and keep warm while you fry the rest.
Serve right away with the garlic sauce and lemon.
Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Add the lukewarm milk and egg and beat to a thick, sticky batter.
Stir in the raisins and chopped apple.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip two spoons in the hot oil, scoop a ball of batter with one and push it off with the other.
Fry 4 or 5 balls at a time for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through (200°F/93°C inside).
Drain the fried balls on a tray lined with paper towels.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm.
